brief.meaningEn: Have more harmful effects than beneficial ones overall.
brief.meaningZh: 整體而言，帶來的壞處比好處更多。
brief.grammar: do more harm than good; inflect do for tense and agreement; often with may/can.
brief.register: Neutral spoken and written English; useful for evaluating a well-intended action.
brief.boundaryZh: 比較整體壞處與好處；不是指完全沒有好處，也不一定涉及身體傷害。
brief.misconceptionZh: 出於好意不代表結果一定有幫助；也不能只因一個小缺點便斷定弊多於利。
brief.outcomeZh: 能解釋為何某種幫忙方法反而造成更大問題。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Book 1 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: That said, I also think the challenge needs to be manageable, because too much pressure can do more harm than good.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 2, table 2, row 2; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: Giving Ella every answer did more harm than good because she stopped trying problems herself.
listening.zh: 把所有答案都告訴 Ella，結果弊多於利，因為她不再自己嘗試解題。
listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣評價這種幫忙方法？

options.en: It made Ella less independent overall.
options.zh: 整體而言，這令 Ella 更欠缺獨立解題能力。

options.en: It caused Ella a physical injury.
options.zh: 這令 Ella 身體受傷。

options.en: It helped Ella learn without any drawbacks.
options.zh: 這幫助 Ella 學習，而且沒有任何壞處。

options.en: It was harmful only because the answers were incorrect.
options.zh: 這種做法有害，唯一原因是答案不正確。

listening.explanationZh: 線索是她不再自行嘗試。這裏比較整體影響，沒有說答案錯誤或身體受傷。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：為甚麼你不直接替他改完整份功課？
reply.promptEn: Why not just correct all his homework for him?

options.en: He needs a chance to spot his own mistakes.
options.zh: 他需要有機會自己找出錯誤。

options.en: Doing everything for him could do more harm than good.
options.zh: 替他包辦一切可能會弊多於利。

options.en: I want to help him learn to work independently.
options.zh: 我想幫他學會獨立完成工作。

options.en: He might rely on me instead of learning the skill.
options.zh: 他可能會依賴我，而不是學會這項技巧。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都能解釋不包辦功課的理由；金句指出這樣幫忙可能整體弊多於利。

scene.promptZh: 同學擔心朋友考試，把朋友每晚的休息時間也排滿練習。朋友反而更累，成績下降。哪句最合適？

options.en: The extra practice may do more harm than good.
options.zh: 額外練習可能會弊多於利。

options.en: The practice has only brought benefits.
options.zh: 練習只有帶來好處。

options.en: The plan cannot affect her performance.
options.zh: 這個計劃不可能影響她的表現。

scene.explanationZh: 練習原本為了幫忙，卻令她過度疲勞、成績下降，支持整體負面評價。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不宜用 do more harm than good 來評價結果？

options.en: A shortcut saves five minutes but regularly loses important files.
options.zh: 一個捷徑能省五分鐘，卻經常令重要檔案遺失。

options.en: A quiet study group helps everyone understand the work and causes no problems.
options.zh: 一個安靜的溫習小組讓大家理解功課，而且沒有造成問題。

options.en: Repeated reminders make a nervous speaker panic and forget her notes.
options.zh: 反覆提醒令緊張的演講者慌亂，忘掉筆記內容。

contrast.explanationZh: 第二個情況只有明確好處，沒有壞處大於好處的證據。

dialogue.promptZh: 同學說：「我想在群組公開指出他的每一個錯誤，這樣他才會進步。」哪個回應最合宜？

options.en: That could do more harm than good. Could you speak to him privately instead?
options.zh: 這樣可能會弊多於利。你可以改為私下跟他談嗎？

options.en: Correcting every mistake publicly is the best way to help him improve.
options.zh: 公開糾正每個錯誤是幫他進步的最佳方法。

options.en: I would wait until the group has finished the project before raising any of the problems.
options.zh: 我會等小組完成專題後，才提出任何問題。

dialogue.explanationZh: 先提醒做法可能有反效果，再提出私下溝通；比公開逐一批評或拖至完成後才提出，更能及時幫助對方。

speaking.en: Checking my messages all night did more harm than good before the exam.
speaking.zh: 考試前整晚查看訊息，結果對我弊多於利。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明考試前整晚查看訊息的整體影響。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友想幫妹妹準備演出，卻不斷在她練習時打斷她，令她更緊張。用一至兩句英文評價這種幫忙，並提出下一步。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出幫忙的整體負面影響，並提出具體替代方法；may 或 could 表示審慎判斷，不需要照抄示例。

examples.en: Constant interruptions may do more harm than good. Let her finish the song first.
examples.zh: 不斷打斷她可能會弊多於利。先讓她唱完整首歌吧。

examples.en: Your advice could do more harm than good if it makes her nervous. Try giving feedback after practice.
examples.zh: 如果你的建議令她緊張，可能會弊多於利。試試在練習後才給意見。

takeaways.en: Too much advice can do more harm than good.
takeaways.zh: 太多建議可能會弊多於利。

takeaways.en: Doing the whole task for her may do more harm than good.
takeaways.zh: 替她完成整個任務可能會弊多於利。

brief.meaningEn: A metaphorical contrast between being challenged constructively and being overwhelmed.
brief.meaningZh: 比喻適量挑戰帶來成長，與過大壓力令人不堪重負的分別。
brief.grammar: Parallel -ing forms being stretched and being crushed can follow between; an explanatory contrast, not a fixed idiom.
brief.register: Reflective discussion about learning or workload; explain the metaphor through context.
brief.boundaryZh: stretched 在此是能力受到挑戰，crushed 是壓力令人難以承受；不是身體被拉長或壓扁。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不舒服不一定等於受到傷害；要看任務是否可應付、有支援和恢復時間。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分辨有助成長的挑戰與令人承受不了的壓力。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Book 1 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: There is a big difference between being stretched and being crushed.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 2, table 2, row 3; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: There is a difference between being stretched and being crushed: this project is difficult, but we have time and support.
listening.zh: 受到挑戰與不堪重負是有分別的：這個專題很難，但我們有時間和支援。
listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣看待目前的專題？

options.en: It is demanding but manageable with support.
options.zh: 它要求較高，但有支援便能應付。

options.en: It has already become too much for the students to manage.
options.zh: 它已經超出學生能應付的程度。

options.en: Its difficulty guarantees that everyone will improve.
options.zh: 它的難度保證每個人都會進步。

options.en: The students have no time or support.
options.zh: 學生沒有時間，也沒有支援。

listening.explanationZh: 後半句明確給出時間與支援，說明這是可應付的挑戰，而非把人壓垮。

reply.promptZh: 同事問：這項新任務很難，我怎樣知道壓力是否過大？
reply.promptEn: This new task is hard. How do I know if the pressure is too much?

options.en: Check whether you have enough support and time to recover.
options.zh: 看看你是否有足夠支援和恢復精神的時間。

options.en: Notice whether the challenge helps you learn or stops you functioning.
options.zh: 留意挑戰是在幫你學習，還是令你連日常工作也做不到。

options.en: There is a difference between being stretched and being crushed; ask for help if you cannot cope.
options.zh: 受到挑戰與不堪重負是有分別的；如果你應付不了，便要求助。

options.en: Talk to your manager if the workload feels too heavy.
options.zh: 如果工作量令你覺得負擔太重，便跟主管談談。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都提供合理判斷或求助方法；金句用平行比喻區分兩種壓力。

scene.promptZh: 一名學生做難題時需要思考，但老師會提示，她也有足夠休息。另一名學生每天做到深夜，沒有支援，已無法集中。哪句最準確？

options.en: Only the amount of work matters; support makes no difference.
options.zh: 只有工作量重要；支援不會帶來分別。

options.en: The contrast illustrates being stretched and being crushed.
options.zh: 這個對比說明了受到挑戰與不堪重負的分別。

options.en: Both students are simply adjusting to a challenge they can handle.
options.zh: 兩名學生都只是在適應一個應付得到的挑戰。

scene.explanationZh: 是否有支援、休息和應付能力，是兩個情況的關鍵分別。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個理解最不符合 being stretched and being crushed 在這裏的比喻？

options.en: A demanding task can help someone develop.
options.zh: 要求較高的任務可以幫助一個人成長。

options.en: Too much pressure can overwhelm someone.
options.zh: 太大壓力可以令人不堪重負。

options.en: The phrase means that all pressure is equally harmful.
options.zh: 這個表達是指所有壓力都同樣有害。

contrast.explanationZh: 這組比喻正是要區分兩種情況，不是把所有壓力一概視為有害。

dialogue.promptZh: 組員說：「這份工作有點難，但我正在學新技巧。」你想確認他是否應付得到。哪句最合適？

options.en: There is a difference between being stretched and being crushed. Do you have the support you need?
options.zh: 受到挑戰與不堪重負是有分別的。你有足夠支援嗎？

options.en: If anything is difficult, it must already be crushing you.
options.zh: 只要有困難，就一定已經把你壓垮。

options.en: Because you are learning, the workload cannot be too much.
options.zh: 因為你正在學習，工作量就不可能過多。

dialogue.explanationZh: 先承認挑戰可以有益，再詢問支援，沒有替對方武斷下結論。

speaking.en: Our tutor explained the difference between being stretched and being crushed.
speaking.zh: 我們的導師解釋了受到挑戰與不堪重負的分別。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說出導師比較的兩種情況。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你帶領義工設計活動。他們希望學新技巧，但目前每晚都工作至深夜。用一至兩句英文說明你會怎樣判斷及調整安排。
writing.selfCheckZh: 區分有益挑戰與過大負擔，並提出工作量、培訓或休息上的調整；不要把任何困難都稱為有害。

examples.en: We need to recognise the difference between being stretched and being crushed. Let's reduce the late-night work.
examples.zh: 我們需要認清受到挑戰與不堪重負的分別。減少深夜工作吧。

examples.en: Being stretched and being crushed are not the same. We should offer training and allow more rest.
examples.zh: 受到挑戰與不堪重負並不相同。我們應提供培訓，並讓大家有更多休息。

takeaways.en: There is a difference between being stretched and being crushed.
takeaways.zh: 受到挑戰與不堪重負是有分別的。

takeaways.en: Our manager understands the difference between being stretched and being crushed.
takeaways.zh: 我們的主管了解受到挑戰與不堪重負的分別。

brief.meaningEn: Make someone very tired by using up their mental or physical energy.
brief.meaningZh: 消耗某人的體力或精神，令人疲憊。
brief.grammar: drain + possessive adjective + energy; drain is transitive and can change tense.
brief.register: Neutral everyday metaphor for tiring work, worry, noise or demands.
brief.boundaryZh: 通常形容逐漸消耗精力，不是從身體抽出真正的液體，也不表示一定失去興趣。
brief.misconceptionZh: 事情可以很有意義，同時令人疲累；消耗精力並不等於討厭那件事。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述甚麼持續消耗精力，並提出恢復或調整的方法。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Book 1 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: But if the pressure is constant, overwhelming, or unrealistic, it can drain their energy and damage their mental health.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 2, table 2, row 4; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The constant noise drains my energy, even when I am doing work I enjoy.
listening.zh: 即使正在做喜歡的工作，持續的噪音也令我精力耗盡。
listening.promptZh: 說話者主要想表達甚麼？

options.en: The speaker has lost interest in the job itself.
options.zh: 說話者對工作本身失去了興趣。

options.en: The noise leaves the speaker feeling tired.
options.zh: 噪音令說話者感到疲累。

options.en: The speaker is mainly worried about making a poor impression.
options.zh: 說話者主要擔心給人留下壞印象。

options.en: The speaker feels busier but just as refreshed.
options.zh: 說話者覺得更忙，但精神仍然一樣充沛。

listening.explanationZh: even when 說明喜歡工作與感到疲累可以同時存在；重點是噪音消耗精力。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：為甚麼你每天開完那幾個會議都那麼累？
reply.promptEn: Why are you so tired after those meetings every day?

options.en: They go on for hours without a break.
options.zh: 那些會議持續幾小時，沒有休息。

options.en: Following several discussions at once is exhausting.
options.zh: 同時跟上幾場討論很累人。

options.en: I spend the whole afternoon focusing on the talks.
options.zh: 我整個下午都要集中精神聽會議上的討論。

options.en: The long meetings drain my energy.
options.zh: 漫長的會議消耗了我的精力。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都能解釋疲累；金句概括持續消耗精力的影響。

scene.promptZh: 你連續幾晚一邊照顧年幼弟弟，一邊完成報告，感到筋疲力盡。哪句最自然？

options.en: The late nights are draining my energy.
options.zh: 連續熬夜正在消耗我的精力。

options.en: I have lost interest in my report and do not want to finish it.
options.zh: 我對報告失去興趣，不想完成它。

options.en: I am mainly frustrated because my brother ignores my advice.
options.zh: 我主要因為弟弟不理會我的建議而感到挫敗。

scene.explanationZh: 連續熬夜造成精力消耗，情境沒有說你對報告失去興趣，也沒有說弟弟不理會建議。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不像 drain their energy？

options.en: Volunteers feel worn out after answering calls for six hours.
options.zh: 義工連續接聽電話六小時後感到疲憊。

options.en: Repeated arguments leave the team mentally exhausted.
options.zh: 反覆爭吵令團隊精神疲累。

options.en: A short walk leaves the students refreshed and ready to study.
options.zh: 短暫散步令學生精神一振，準備好溫習。

contrast.explanationZh: 精神一振與精力受到消耗相反。不能只因有活動便使用這個表達。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我很喜歡這個義工項目，但已經連續十天沒有休息。」哪個回應最體貼？

options.en: If you enjoy it, it cannot possibly make you tired.
options.zh: 如果你喜歡它，就絕不可能令你疲累。

options.en: It may still drain your energy. Could you take a day off?
options.zh: 它仍可能消耗你的精力。你可以休息一天嗎？

options.en: Feeling tired proves that the project is pointless.
options.zh: 感到疲累證明這個項目毫無意義。

dialogue.explanationZh: 承認有意義的事情也會令人疲累，再提出休息的可能性。

speaking.en: Answering messages during every break drained my energy.
speaking.zh: 每次休息都回覆訊息，消耗了我的精力。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明這種休息習慣對精力有甚麼影響。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你的同學連續幾天晚上都在吵鬧的客廳溫習，現在很疲倦。用一至兩句英文描述問題，並提出改善方法。
writing.selfCheckZh: 描述噪音如何令人疲累，並提出一項可行改變；不用把疲累誤寫成不喜歡學習。

examples.en: Studying in a noisy room drains her energy. She could try the library tomorrow.
examples.zh: 在吵鬧的房間溫習消耗她的精力。她明天可以試試去圖書館。

examples.en: The constant noise is draining her energy, so she should find a quieter place to study.
examples.zh: 持續的噪音正在消耗她的精力，所以她應找一個較安靜的地方溫習。

takeaways.en: Constant interruptions can drain your energy.
takeaways.zh: 不斷受到打擾會消耗你的精力。

takeaways.en: A long argument can drain my energy even when the issue matters to me.
takeaways.zh: 即使事情對我很重要，長時間爭論仍會消耗我的精力。

brief.meaningEn: An explicit comparison with physical training; context supplies the shared quality.
brief.meaningZh: 把某件事比作體能鍛鍊；相似之處要由上下文說明。
brief.grammar: X is (a bit) like exercise: followed by the reason. Exercise is uncountable in this general sense.
brief.register: Explanatory simile, not a fixed idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: 可以比較循序漸進、持續練習或適量休息，但不能把所有運動特點硬套進去。
brief.misconceptionZh: 明喻不表示被比較的事情真的是體育活動，也不是只限於挑戰的慣用語。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用清楚的共同點，把抽象的學習過程比作鍛鍊。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Book 1 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: To me, challenge is a bit like exercise: the right amount makes you stronger, but too much can leave you injured.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 3, table 1, row 2; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: Building confidence is like exercise: small, regular efforts matter more than one huge effort.
listening.zh: 建立自信就像鍛鍊一樣：持續的小努力，比一次極大的努力更重要。

options.en: Confidence grows mainly through physical fitness.
options.zh: 自信主要透過體能提升而建立。

options.en: One enormous effort always replaces regular practice.
options.zh: 一次極大的努力總能取代持續練習。

options.en: Repeated manageable efforts help confidence grow.
options.zh: 持續而可應付的努力有助建立自信。

options.en: Taking on the hardest challenge immediately is the fastest route.
options.zh: 立即接受最難的挑戰是最快的方法。

listening.explanationZh: 冒號後說明相似點是持續的小努力；比較不等於兩件事在每方面都一樣。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：為甚麼每天練五分鐘演講，而不是每月才練一次很久？
reply.promptEn: Why practise speaking for five minutes every day instead of one long session a month?

options.en: It is like exercise: a little regular practice helps me improve.
options.zh: 這就像鍛鍊一樣：持續練習一點點，有助我進步。

options.en: Short daily sessions are easier for me to maintain.
options.zh: 每天短時間練習較容易持續。

options.en: I remember the skills better when I use them often.
options.zh: 經常運用這些技巧，我會記得更牢。

options.en: A steady routine helps me build confidence gradually.
options.zh: 穩定的習慣幫我逐漸建立自信。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都說明持續練習的價值；金句用有解釋的明喻作比較。

scene.promptZh: 老師想解釋學習解難需要由簡入深，不能第一天就做最難任務。哪句比喻最清楚？

options.en: Problem-solving is like exercise: start gently and increase the difficulty gradually.
options.zh: 解難就像鍛鍊一樣：先從輕量開始，再逐漸增加難度。

options.en: Problem-solving is like exercise: you should begin with the hardest task to make faster progress.
options.zh: 解難就像鍛鍊一樣：你應從最難的任務開始，以便更快進步。

options.en: Problem-solving is like exercise: natural talent matters more than guided practice.
options.zh: 解難就像鍛鍊一樣：天分比有指導的練習更重要。

scene.explanationZh: 循序漸進是語境中兩件事的共同點；示範比較的重點是有系統地累積技巧。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個說法最不符合這種明喻的用法？

options.en: Both activities may need regular practice.
options.zh: 兩種活動都可能需要持續練習。

options.en: Every feature of physical training must also apply to learning.
options.zh: 體能鍛鍊的每個特點都必須適用於學習。

options.en: The writer should explain the similarity.
options.zh: 作者應解釋相似之處。

contrast.explanationZh: 明喻選取相關的相似點，不能據此推論所有特點完全相同。

dialogue.promptZh: 同學說：「我練寫作兩天，為甚麼還未很厲害？」哪句最能鼓勵他並解釋原因？

options.en: Writing is like exercise: regular practice builds skill over time.
options.zh: 寫作就像鍛鍊一樣：持續練習會隨時間建立能力。

options.en: Writing is like exercise: one very long session should replace a regular habit.
options.zh: 寫作就像鍛鍊一樣：一次很長的練習應取代固定習慣。

options.en: Writing improves as soon as you buy the right equipment.
options.zh: 只要買對工具，寫作便會立即進步。

dialogue.explanationZh: 以長期練習這個共同點作解釋，也避免不切實際的保證。

speaking.en: Learning to listen carefully is like exercise: regular practice makes a difference.
speaking.zh: 學習用心聆聽就像鍛鍊一樣：持續練習會帶來改變。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再用明喻說明用心聆聽需要持續練習。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友只在比賽前一天練習記憶，卻希望立刻進步。用一至兩句英文，以鍛鍊作比較，建議他建立日常練習。
writing.selfCheckZh: 說明明確共同點，例如持續、循序漸進；不要只有比較而沒有解釋。

examples.en: Training your memory is like exercise: short daily sessions help you improve gradually.
examples.zh: 訓練記憶就像鍛鍊一樣：每天短時間練習，有助你逐漸進步。

examples.en: Memory training is like exercise. Try a little practice every day rather than one long session.
examples.zh: 記憶訓練就像鍛鍊一樣。試試每天練一點，而不是只作一次長時間練習。

takeaways.en: Learning a skill can be like exercise: regular practice helps.
takeaways.zh: 學習技巧可以像鍛鍊一樣：持續練習會有幫助。

takeaways.en: Improving your memory is like exercise: small, regular sessions can help.
takeaways.zh: 改善記憶就像鍛鍊一樣：持續作短時間練習會有幫助。

brief.meaningEn: Cause someone to be injured as a result; physical injury in exercise, with a possible metaphorical extension to serious harm in other contexts.
brief.meaningZh: 造成某人受傷的結果；運動中通常指身體傷害，在明確比喻中也可延伸為嚴重傷害。
brief.grammar: leave + object + injured; past tense left. The adjective describes the resulting state, not a location.
brief.register: Natural literal resultative construction. Figurative use requires a clear comparison; hurt is often plainer for emotional effects.
brief.boundaryZh: 原文用運動可能受傷，比喻過量挑戰的傷害。教學先確立自然的字面句式，再解釋比喻；一般疲累不等於受傷。
brief.misconceptionZh: leave 不是離開，也不代表故意傷人；injured 與 tired 的程度和意思不同。
brief.outcomeZh: 能理解造成傷害的結果句式，並區分身體受傷、一般疲累與上下文支持的比喻。
brief.sourceClassificationNote: Source classified the exercise/challenge analogy as figurative. The dominant taught construction leave + object + injured is a natural literal resultative; an explicit just-as comparison preserves and explains the original figurative extension.

sources.sentence: To me, challenge is a bit like exercise: the right amount makes you stronger, but too much can leave you injured.

listening.en: A demanding training plan can leave you injured rather than simply tired if it pushes you beyond your limits.
listening.zh: 如果高要求的訓練計劃把你推至極限之外，可能令你受傷，而不只是疲累。
listening.promptZh: 說話者如何區分受傷與一般疲累？

options.en: The plan could cause harm beyond ordinary tiredness.
options.zh: 計劃可能造成超出一般疲累程度的傷害。

options.en: Feeling tired always proves that an injury has occurred.
options.zh: 感到疲累永遠證明已經受傷。

options.en: The plan is described as completely safe for everyone.
options.zh: 計劃被形容為對每個人都完全安全。

options.en: The person has already decided to leave the team.
options.zh: 那個人已決定離開團隊。

listening.explanationZh: rather than simply tired 區分兩種結果；can 表示可能，沒有斷言已經發生傷勢。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：為甚麼你想調整這個要求過高的訓練計劃？
reply.promptEn: Why do you want to change this overly demanding training plan?

options.en: It gives beginners no time to recover.
options.zh: 它沒有給初學者恢復的時間。

options.en: I am concerned that the workload is beyond their limits.
options.zh: 我擔心訓練量超出他們能承受的程度。

options.en: It could leave you injured instead of helping you improve.
options.zh: 它可能令你受傷，而不是幫助你進步。

options.en: We need a safer plan that beginners can manage.
options.zh: 我們需要一個初學者應付得到、較安全的計劃。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都解釋調整計劃的合理理由；金句表達可能造成受傷的結果，不是離開地方。

scene.promptZh: 文章已把過量工作比作過度運動。哪句最清楚延續這個比喻，同時避免把普通疲累說成真的受傷？

options.en: Just as excessive training can leave you injured, an impossible workload can cause lasting harm.
options.zh: 正如過度訓練可能令你受傷，不可能完成的工作量也可能造成持續傷害。

options.en: Being tired after any task proves that you have been injured.
options.zh: 做完任何任務後疲累，就證明你已受傷。

options.en: Every challenge causes exactly the same harm as a physical accident.
options.zh: 每個挑戰都會造成跟身體意外完全相同的傷害。

scene.explanationZh: just as 明示比較，can 表示可能；這樣描述共同的受傷風險，沒有把疲累當成傷勢。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不宜用 leave you injured 來形容？

options.en: An accident during a match causes a physical injury.
options.zh: 比賽中的意外造成身體受傷。

options.en: A writer explicitly compares lasting emotional harm with a wound.
options.zh: 作者明確把持續的情緒傷害比作傷口。

options.en: A short rehearsal makes you slightly tired, with no harm or injury described.
options.zh: 短暫排練令你稍微疲累，沒有描述傷害或傷勢。

contrast.explanationZh: 一般疲累不等於受傷。比喻義需要清楚語境，不能把 injured 當作 tired 的普通替換字。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「練習後有點累，就是 injured 嗎？」哪個回應最準確？

options.en: Not necessarily. A task can make you tired without leaving you injured.
options.zh: 不一定。任務可以令你疲累，但沒有令你受傷。

options.en: Yes. Injured and tired mean exactly the same thing.
options.zh: 對。injured 和 tired 意思完全相同。

options.en: Injured means that you decided to leave the place.
options.zh: injured 表示你決定離開那個地方。

dialogue.explanationZh: 清楚區分疲累與受傷；leave + object + injured 表達結果，不是地點。

speaking.en: An unrealistic training plan could leave you injured rather than help you improve.
speaking.zh: 不切實際的訓練計劃可能令你受傷，而不是幫助你進步。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明不切實際訓練計劃可能造成的結果。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：舞蹈小組安排新手每天作遠超能力的訓練，而且沒有休息時間。你想提醒組長：這不只是令人疲累。用一至兩句英文指出可能的傷害，並建議調整計劃。

examples.en: This excessive training could leave you injured, not just tired. We need a safer plan.
examples.zh: 這種過量訓練可能令你受傷，不只是疲累。我們需要一個較安全的計劃。

examples.en: Pushing beginners beyond their limits may leave them injured. The group should review the plan with a qualified instructor.
examples.zh: 把初學者推至極限之外可能令他們受傷。小組應與合資格導師一起檢視計劃。

writing.selfCheckZh: 表達可能造成的傷害，區分 injured 與 tired；提出檢視或調整安排，不要聲稱已經發生未經確認的傷勢。

takeaways.en: Excessive training can leave you injured rather than simply tired.
takeaways.zh: 過量訓練可能令你受傷，而不只是疲累。

takeaways.en: An excessive workload is like training that can leave you injured: the challenge can become harmful.
takeaways.zh: 過量工作就像可能令你受傷的訓練：挑戰可以變成傷害。

options.en: We are training staff to respond more quickly.
options.zh: 我們正在培訓員工加快回應。

options.en: We have checked the menu and improved the service.
options.zh: 我們檢查了菜單，也改善了服務。

options.en: We need to raise our game and make every visit better.
options.zh: 我們需要提升表現，令每次到訪的體驗更好。

options.en: We are working on the details that guests notice.
options.zh: 我們正在改善客人會留意的細節。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都合理；金句概括提升整體表現，不是只增加工作量。

options.en: They lowered their standards because the opponents were strong.
options.zh: 因為對手很強，他們降低了標準。

scene.explanationZh: 有具體技巧改善及進步證據，符合提高表現的比喻。

options.en: A team repeats the same mistakes and accepts a lower standard.

options.en: A player improves her accuracy before the final.

options.zh: 我們練習處理棘手的顧客情況，提升表現吧。

options.en: Let's keep the same routine and wait until someone complains.
options.zh: 我們維持原來的做法，等有人投訴再說吧。

options.en: Let us book more tables without changing how we serve them.
options.zh: 我們多接幾枱預訂，但不用改變服務方法。

dialogue.explanationZh: 針對較高的服務標準，練習處理棘手情況能提升表現；單純增加客人數目或等人投訴，都沒有改善服務。

speaking.en: I raised my game by asking for detailed feedback on each presentation.
speaking.zh: 我每次演講後都尋求詳細意見，藉此提升表現。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明你如何提升演講表現。

titleEn: knock the wind out of them

brief.meaningEn: Suddenly take away someone’s confidence or enthusiasm; literally, make someone unable to breathe briefly after an impact.
brief.meaningZh: 突然打擊某人的信心或幹勁；字面上可指受到撞擊後一時喘不過氣。
brief.grammar: knock the wind out of + object pronoun/name; past knocked.
brief.register: Vivid conversational idiom; context distinguishes emotional setback from physical impact.
brief.boundaryZh: 比喻用法通常有突然的壞消息或挫折，不只是逐漸感到疲累。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不一定真的發生撞擊，也不表示受挫後永遠無法恢復。
brief.outcomeZh: 能形容突如其來的挫折如何打擊信心。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Book 1 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.expression: knock the wind out of them
sources.sentence: By contrast, giving them an impossible workload with no support may simply knock the wind out of them.

listening.en: Having our proposal rejected without explanation knocked the wind out of us for a while.
listening.zh: 我們的建議在沒有獲得解釋的情況下被拒絕，令我們一時大受打擊。

options.en: A sudden loss of confidence after disappointing news.
options.zh: 失望消息帶來的突然信心打擊。

options.en: A long period of routine work had gradually tired them out.
options.zh: 一段漫長的例行工作逐漸令他們疲累。

options.en: A slow improvement in the proposal.
options.zh: 建議逐漸得到改善。

options.en: A decision never to work together again.
options.zh: 永遠不再合作的決定。

listening.explanationZh: 沒有身體撞擊；被拒絕的消息令團隊一時受挫，for a while 也沒有說永遠放棄。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：為甚麼收到拒絕通知後，你突然那麼沉默？
reply.promptEn: Why did you suddenly go quiet after the rejection arrived?

options.en: I was disappointed because I had worked so hard on it.
options.zh: 我很失望，因為我為此付出很多努力。

options.en: The rejection knocked the wind out of me, and I needed a moment.
options.zh: 被拒絕令我大受打擊，需要一點時間緩過來。

options.en: I had expected a different result and did not know what to say.
options.zh: 我原本期待不同結果，一時不知道說甚麼。

options.en: I was trying to take in the disappointing news.
options.zh: 我在嘗試消化這個令人失望的消息。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都解釋沉默；金句強調突如其來的信心打擊。

scene.promptZh: 學生辛苦準備的作品突然被取消參賽資格，她一時失去幹勁。哪句最準確？

options.en: The news knocked the wind out of her.
options.zh: 這個消息令她大受打擊。

options.en: The news proves she will never recover.
options.zh: 這個消息證明她永遠無法恢復。

options.en: She felt relieved because the competition was no longer important.
options.zh: 她鬆了一口氣，因為比賽不再重要。

scene.explanationZh: 突如其來的失望和幹勁下降支持比喻用法，卻不足以判斷長期結果。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不像比喻中的 knock the wind out of them？

options.en: An unexpected cancellation leaves performers stunned and discouraged.
options.zh: 演出突然取消，令表演者震驚和氣餒。

options.en: A harsh rejection suddenly shakes the team's confidence.
options.zh: 嚴厲拒絕突然打擊團隊信心。

options.en: A familiar walk gradually makes the group pleasantly tired.
options.zh: 熟悉的散步令大家逐漸有點舒適的疲倦。

contrast.explanationZh: 逐漸疲倦沒有突然挫折及信心打擊的意思。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「落選真的令我很難受，我現在甚麼也不想做。」哪句最體貼？

options.en: I can see it knocked the wind out of you. Would you like some time before we talk?
options.zh: 我看得出這令你大受打擊。你想先休息一下再談嗎？

options.en: You will feel better only if you start another entry immediately.
options.zh: 你只有立即開始另一份參賽作品才會好受一點。

options.en: It means nothing, so stop feeling disappointed.
options.zh: 這毫無意義，別再失望了。

dialogue.explanationZh: 承認受挫感受並給予空間，不誇大為永遠失敗，也不否定感受。

speaking.en: The sudden cancellation knocked the wind out of me, but I made another plan.
speaking.zh: 突然取消的消息令我大受打擊，但我另訂了計劃。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明消息如何突然打擊你。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你和朋友準備多月的展覽因場地關閉而突然取消。用一至兩句英文說明消息對你們的打擊，以及一個可行的下一步。
writing.selfCheckZh: 交代突然受挫與幹勁下降，並寫出實際下一步；不用暗示永遠無法恢復。

examples.en: The cancellation knocked the wind out of us. We could look for another venue next week.
examples.zh: 取消的消息令我們大受打擊。我們下星期可以找另一個場地。

examples.en: Losing the exhibition space knocked the wind out of us, but we will contact a local library.
examples.zh: 失去展覽場地令我們大受打擊，但我們會聯絡一間區內圖書館。

takeaways.en: The rejection knocked the wind out of me for a moment.
takeaways.zh: 被拒絕令我一時大受打擊。

takeaways.en: The cancellation knocked the wind out of us, but we found another venue.
takeaways.zh: 取消的消息令我們大受打擊，但我們找到了另一個場地。

brief.meaningEn: Challenge someone enough to develop without overwhelming or harming them.
brief.meaningZh: 給人足以成長的挑戰，而不是把人壓垮。
brief.grammar: stretch + object, not break + matching object; a contextual metaphorical contrast, not a fixed idiom.
brief.register: Encouraging discussion of teaching, coaching or workload.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是保證任務輕鬆；要保留挑戰，同時有合理難度與支援。
brief.misconceptionZh: not break 不等於完全不讓人遇到困難，也不是把人的身體當成物件。
brief.outcomeZh: 能提出有挑戰但可應付的學習或工作安排。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Book 1 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Overall, I do believe people need to be challenged, but the challenge should stretch them, not break them.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 3, table 1, row 6; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The new assignments should stretch them, not break them, so we are adding support sessions.
listening.zh: 新功課應給他們挑戰，而不是把他們壓垮，所以我們會加設支援時段。
listening.promptZh: 說話者希望怎樣安排功課？

options.en: Remove every demanding task.
options.zh: 取消所有有要求的任務。

options.en: Keep the challenge but provide enough support.
options.zh: 保留挑戰，但提供足夠支援。

options.en: Make the tasks impossible to complete.
options.zh: 令任務不可能完成。

options.en: Increase the workload until students stop asking questions.
options.zh: 增加工作量，直到學生不再提問。

listening.explanationZh: 加設支援時段，說明仍保留挑戰，但避免過度負荷。

reply.promptZh: 同事問：這項培訓應該有多難？
reply.promptEn: How difficult should this training be?

options.en: It should give beginners a challenge they can manage.
options.zh: 它應給初學者一個應付得到的挑戰。

options.en: We should build in guidance and time to practise.
options.zh: 我們應安排指導和練習時間。

options.en: It should stretch them, not break them.
options.zh: 它應給他們挑戰，而不是把他們壓垮。

options.en: The difficulty should increase as their skills develop.
options.zh: 難度應隨他們的技巧進步而增加。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都描述合理培訓；金句以對比說明挑戰與過度負荷的界線。

scene.promptZh: 舞蹈老師設計稍有難度的新動作，分段教學並安排休息，目的是讓學生進步而不超出負荷。哪句最合適？

options.en: The lessons should stretch them, not break them.
options.zh: 課堂應給他們挑戰，而不是把他們壓垮。

options.en: The lessons should contain no new skills at all.
options.zh: 課堂完全不應有新技巧。

options.en: Support would prevent all improvement.
options.zh: 支援會阻止所有進步。

scene.explanationZh: 新技巧有挑戰，分段教學和休息提供支援，符合比喻的兩面。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個安排最不符合 stretch them, not break them？

options.en: A difficult task with coaching and a realistic deadline.
options.zh: 有指導和合理限期的困難任務。

options.en: A gradual increase in responsibility with regular check-ins.
options.zh: 逐步增加責任，並定期了解情況。

options.en: An impossible deadline, no guidance and punishment for asking questions.
options.zh: 不可能完成的限期、沒有指導，提問還要受罰。

contrast.explanationZh: 第三個安排只增加負擔而不提供應付條件，違反避免壓垮人的原則。

dialogue.promptZh: 導師說：「我想幫新組員成長，但他們剛入門。」哪句最有用？

options.en: Give them every difficult task at once and offer no help.
options.zh: 立刻把所有難題交給他們，也不要幫忙。

options.en: Choose tasks that stretch them, not break them, and check in regularly.
options.zh: 選擇能挑戰他們而不把他們壓垮的任務，並定期了解情況。

options.en: Avoid teaching anything they do not already know.
options.zh: 不要教任何他們還未懂的東西。

dialogue.explanationZh: 兼顧成長、合理難度與持續支援，不落入毫無挑戰或過度負荷的兩端。

speaking.en: These projects should stretch us, not break us, and we can ask for guidance.
speaking.zh: 這些專題應給我們挑戰，而不是把我們壓垮，而且我們可以尋求指導。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再以對比說明專題應達到的效果。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你安排新義工第一次主持活動，想讓他們練習，但不想一次交給他們太多責任。用一至兩句英文說明原則及支援方法。
writing.selfCheckZh: 同時保留挑戰與可應付的條件；用具體支援方法解釋，不能只說不要有困難。

examples.en: The role should stretch them, not break them. An experienced volunteer can help with difficult moments.
examples.zh: 這個角色應給他們挑戰，而不是把他們壓垮。有經驗的義工可以協助處理困難時刻。

examples.en: We want to stretch them, not break them, so we will start with a short activity and provide guidance.
examples.zh: 我們想給他們挑戰，而不是把他們壓垮，所以會先安排短活動，並提供指導。

takeaways.en: A good challenge should stretch you, not break you.
takeaways.zh: 好的挑戰應讓你成長，而不是把你壓垮。

takeaways.en: We choose projects that stretch them, not break them.
takeaways.zh: 我們選擇能給他們挑戰、卻不會把他們壓垮的專題。

titleEn: bring out the best in people

target.pattern: \b(?:bring|brings|bringing|brought) out the best in (?:me|you|him|her|us|them|people|everyone|a team|the team)\b

brief.meaningEn: Encourage someone’s strongest qualities or abilities to become apparent.
brief.meaningZh: 激發一個人最好的特質或能力。
brief.grammar: bring out the best in + person/group; past brought. Keep out the best in in that order. A team is also a natural group object; the expression is not limited to an individual.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是保證每個結果完美，也不是只稱讚外貌；要有特質或能力得到展現的意思。
brief.misconceptionZh: bring out the best in someone 與把物件拿到外面不同，也不表示強迫人與別人競爭。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述甚麼環境或人能讓別人展現優點。

listening.en: The patient mentor brought out the best in the team by making everyone feel safe to share ideas.
listening.zh: 有耐性的導師令大家放心分享想法，激發了團隊最好的能力。

options.en: She made the team compete without sharing.
options.zh: 她令團隊互相競爭，不再分享。

options.en: She praised every idea equally without listening to the team.
options.zh: 她沒有聆聽團隊，便同樣稱讚每個想法。

options.en: She helped the team show its strengths.
options.zh: 她幫助團隊展現長處。

options.en: She selected the strongest members and ignored the quieter ones.
options.zh: 她挑選最強的組員，忽略較安靜的組員。

listening.explanationZh: 安全分享的環境讓團隊展現能力；沒有保證每個想法完美。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：為甚麼大家都喜歡跟那位導師合作？
reply.promptEn: Why does everyone enjoy working with that mentor?

options.en: She listens carefully and encourages useful ideas.
options.zh: 她用心聆聽，也鼓勵有用的想法。

options.en: She helps quiet people feel confident enough to contribute.
options.zh: 她幫助安靜的人建立信心參與。

options.en: People can show their strengths around her.
options.zh: 大家在她身邊能展現長處。

options.en: She brings out the best in people.
options.zh: 她能激發人們最好的特質。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都合理解釋受歡迎的原因；金句概括她激發別人優點的作用。

scene.promptZh: 原本不敢發言的組員，在組長耐心鼓勵後提出很好的方案，其他人也更願意合作。哪句最合適？

options.en: The leader brought out the best in the team.
options.zh: 組長激發了團隊最好的能力。

options.en: The leader made everyone compete for attention instead of sharing.
options.zh: 組長令大家爭取注意，而不是分享。

options.en: The leader gave praise without creating chances for anyone to contribute.
options.zh: 組長只給予稱讚，沒有讓任何人有機會參與。

scene.explanationZh: 具體優點得到展現，包括提出方案與合作，支持這個正面表達。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不符合 bring out the best in people？

options.en: A tutor's encouragement helps students think independently.
options.zh: 導師的鼓勵幫助學生獨立思考。

options.en: A manager's insults make capable staff hide their ideas.
options.zh: 主管辱罵員工，令有能力的員工不敢提出想法。

options.en: A friendly team helps a shy member share her expertise.
options.zh: 友善的團隊幫助害羞的成員分享專長。

contrast.explanationZh: 第二個情況壓抑長處，與激發最佳一面相反。

dialogue.promptZh: 同事說：「她換了組別後變得很積極，也主動幫人。」哪句自然回應？

options.en: The supportive team seems to bring out the best in her.
options.zh: 這個有支援的團隊似乎激發了她最好的一面。

options.en: That proves she never had any strengths before.
options.zh: 這證明她以前完全沒有長處。

options.en: Her improvement means the team no longer needs to support her.
options.zh: 她有所進步，就表示團隊不用再支援她。

dialogue.explanationZh: seems to 保留合理推斷，指出環境讓原有長處展現，不否定以前的能力。

speaking.en: Working with thoughtful classmates brings out the best in me.
speaking.zh: 跟體貼的同學合作，能激發我最好的一面。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明合作環境如何讓你的優點展現。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：一名很安靜的同學加入友善的戲劇小組後，開始提出創意，也願意幫助其他人。用一至兩句英文描述小組的影響。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出優點或能力如何展現，避免只說她很開心或保證一切完美。

examples.en: The welcoming group brings out the best in her. She now shares creative ideas and helps other members.
examples.zh: 這個友善接納她的小組激發了她最好的一面。她現在會分享創意，也會幫助其他組員。

examples.en: Working with supportive people has brought out the best in her, giving her the confidence to contribute.
examples.zh: 跟有支援態度的人合作，激發了她最好的一面，給了她參與的信心。

takeaways.en: A supportive teacher can bring out the best in people.
takeaways.zh: 願意支持學生的老師能激發人們最好的一面。

takeaways.en: Working with patient colleagues brings out the best in me.
takeaways.zh: 跟有耐性的同事合作，能激發我最好的一面。

brief.meaningEn: Influence how something develops or how someone thinks or behaves.
brief.meaningZh: 影響某件事的發展，或一個人的想法與行為。
brief.grammar: shape + object, such as choices, attitudes or expectations; shaped, shaping.
brief.boundaryZh: 影響不等於完全控制，也不保證是唯一原因；此處不是把實物捏成形狀。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能因廣告有影響便說觀眾沒有選擇；shape 可指多種因素逐漸形成看法。
brief.outcomeZh: 能解釋經歷或資訊如何影響想法與選擇。

sources.sentence: Stories can shape how people feel about history.

listening.en: Stories from her grandparents shaped the way Mina thought about the city.
listening.zh: 祖父母的故事影響了 Mina 看待這座城市的方式。

options.en: They settled every question Mina had about the city.
options.zh: 它們解決了 Mina 對城市的每個疑問。

options.en: They influenced Mina's view of the city.
options.zh: 它們影響了 Mina 對城市的看法。

options.en: They forced every resident to think the same way.
options.zh: 它們迫使所有居民有相同想法。

options.en: They had no connection with her opinions.
options.zh: 它們跟她的看法毫無關係。

listening.explanationZh: 受影響的是她思考城市的方式；不是實際城市形狀，也不是完全控制所有人。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：為甚麼你現在那麼重視無障礙設計？
reply.promptEn: Why do you care so much about accessible design now?

options.en: Helping my neighbour changed what I notice in public spaces.
options.zh: 幫助鄰居改變了我在公共空間會留意的事情。

options.en: I learned how difficult everyday journeys can be.
options.zh: 我了解到日常出行也可能很困難。

options.en: That experience shaped my understanding of accessibility.
options.zh: 那次經歷塑造了我對無障礙設計的理解。

options.en: I began to see the barriers that I had overlooked.
options.zh: 我開始看見以前忽略的障礙。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都解釋看法的來源；金句表達經歷對理解的影響。

scene.promptZh: 學生長期聽到同學談升學，以往沒考慮過的科目也開始進入他的選擇。哪句最準確？

options.en: Those conversations helped shape his choices.
options.zh: 那些對話有助塑造他的選擇。

options.en: Those conversations removed his ability to choose.
options.zh: 那些對話令他失去選擇能力。

options.en: Those conversations left him with no interests.
options.zh: 那些對話令他變得毫無興趣。

scene.explanationZh: 談話是影響因素之一；helped shape 不聲稱完全控制他的選擇。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句最清楚使用 shape 的「影響想法或發展」比喻義？

options.en: She shaped the clay into a bowl.
options.zh: 她把陶土塑造成碗。

options.en: Her first job shaped her attitude towards teamwork.
options.zh: 她的第一份工作塑造了她對團隊合作的態度。

options.en: The artist shaped a piece of wire into a circle.
options.zh: 藝術家把一段金屬線彎成圓形。

contrast.explanationZh: 態度是抽象對象；陶土和金屬線是實際改變形狀的字面用法。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「你的看法是家庭影響的，所以你完全沒有自己的選擇。」哪句最準確回應？

options.en: Family experiences can shape my views without deciding everything for me.
options.zh: 家庭經歷可以影響我的看法，但不會替我決定一切。

options.en: If something shapes my views, I cannot think independently.
options.zh: 只要有事情影響我的看法，我就不能獨立思考。

options.en: Family experiences only matter if I agree with everything I hear.
options.zh: 只有我贊同聽到的一切，家庭經歷才會有影響。

dialogue.explanationZh: 承認影響，同時區分影響與決定一切，符合這個動詞的比喻義。

speaking.en: My first volunteer project shaped my ideas about responsibility.
speaking.zh: 我的第一個義工項目塑造了我對責任的看法。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明義工經歷如何影響你的看法。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你曾跟年長鄰居一起參加社區活動，現在更重視耐心聆聽。用一至兩句英文說明那次經歷對你看法的影響。
writing.selfCheckZh: 說明經歷與現在想法的連結；不必聲稱這是唯一影響，也不要誤寫成實物改變形狀。

examples.en: Working with my older neighbour shaped my view of good communication. I now listen more patiently.
examples.zh: 跟年長鄰居合作，塑造了我對良好溝通的看法。我現在會更耐心聆聽。

examples.en: That community project shaped the way I think about listening, because I learned to give people time.
examples.zh: 那個社區項目影響了我看待聆聽的方式，因為我學會給別人時間。

takeaways.en: Our experiences shape the way we see the world.
takeaways.zh: 我們的經歷塑造了我們看待世界的方式。

takeaways.en: The people we meet can shape our expectations.
takeaways.zh: 我們遇到的人可以塑造我們的期望。

brief.meaningEn: Feel attracted to someone or something.

listening.en: I felt drawn to the photography club because the members noticed beauty in ordinary places.
listening.zh: 我被攝影學會吸引，因為會員能在平凡地方看見美。
listening.promptZh: 說話者對攝影學會有甚麼感覺？

options.en: The speaker felt obliged to join despite having no interest.
options.zh: 說話者雖然沒有興趣，仍覺得有義務加入。

options.en: The speaker disliked everything about the club.
options.zh: 說話者不喜歡學會的一切。

options.en: The speaker felt interested in the club's approach.
options.zh: 說話者被學會看事物的方式吸引。

options.en: The speaker had already become the club president.
options.zh: 說話者已經成為學會主席。

listening.explanationZh: 因為會員的觀察方式而感興趣，不代表已加入或擔任職位。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：為甚麼你一直留意那個設計課程？
reply.promptEn: Why do you keep looking at that design course?

options.en: The practical projects really interest me.
options.zh: 那些實用專題令我很感興趣。

options.en: I feel drawn to its focus on everyday problems.
options.zh: 它重視日常問題這一點令我感到被吸引。

options.en: I like the way students test their ideas.
options.zh: 我喜歡學生測試想法的方式。

options.en: It looks like a good chance to explore my interests.
options.zh: 它看來是探索自己興趣的好機會。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都能解釋興趣；金句使用 feel drawn to，但不聲稱已報名。

scene.promptZh: 你瀏覽幾個義工計劃，對陪長者聊天的項目特別感興趣，但還未報名。哪句最準確？

options.en: I feel drawn to the project, though I have not signed up yet.
options.zh: 我被這個項目吸引，但還未報名。

options.en: I have already committed to the project and no longer need to decide.
options.zh: 我已經承諾參加項目，不用再作決定。

options.en: I only considered the project because someone required me to.
options.zh: 我只是因為有人要求，才考慮這個項目。

scene.explanationZh: 感到吸引與實際報名是不同階段。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不符合 feel drawn to 的意思？

options.en: A student wants to explore a subject that fascinates her.
options.zh: 學生想探索令她着迷的科目。

options.en: A visitor is interested in a quiet garden and wants to look around.
options.zh: 訪客對安靜的花園感興趣，想四處看看。

options.en: A worker has no interest in a task and does it only because it is compulsory.
options.zh: 員工對任務毫無興趣，只因是強制安排才做。

contrast.explanationZh: 第三個情況只有義務，沒有吸引力。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「你對那所學校有興趣，就表示你已經決定入讀吧？」哪個回應最準確？

options.en: I feel drawn to it, but I still need to compare the courses.
options.zh: 我對它感到興趣，但仍需要比較課程。

options.en: Feeling drawn to something always means you have made a final decision.
options.zh: 感到被吸引永遠表示已作最終決定。

options.en: I cannot be interested until I have already enrolled.
options.zh: 我必須已經入讀，才可以感興趣。

dialogue.explanationZh: 承認吸引力，同時清楚表達尚未決定。

speaking.en: I feel drawn to work that lets me help people solve practical problems.
speaking.zh: 能讓我幫助別人解決實際問題的工作，令我感到被吸引。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明甚麼類型的工作吸引你。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你看到一個週末陶藝課程，喜歡親手製作實用品，但尚未決定報名。用一至兩句英文描述興趣及下一步。
writing.selfCheckZh: 描述真實吸引力及原因，並清楚區分感興趣與已作決定。

examples.en: I feel drawn to the pottery course because I enjoy making useful things. I will check the timetable first.
examples.zh: 我被陶藝課程吸引，因為我喜歡製作實用品。我會先查看時間表。

examples.en: I am feeling drawn to pottery, but I want to try a short workshop before I sign up.
examples.zh: 我開始被陶藝吸引，但想先試一個短工作坊，再決定報名。

takeaways.en: I feel drawn to projects that connect people.
takeaways.zh: 能連繫人與人的項目令我感到被吸引。

takeaways.en: She felt drawn to the course but wanted more information before enrolling.
takeaways.zh: 她被課程吸引，但想先了解更多資料再報名。

titleEn: plant a seed in their mind

brief.meaningEn: Introduce an idea or interest that may develop later.
brief.meaningZh: 讓某人初次產生一個想法或興趣，日後可能發展。
brief.grammar: plant a/the seed, optionally followed by of + an idea/interest or in + possessive adjective + mind/minds; tense varies. The idea/interest-growth metaphor remains the same; the definite article can refer to the beginning of a specified later interest.
brief.register: Conventional metaphor in conversation and reflective writing.
brief.boundaryZh: 強調想法的開始與日後可能發展，不保證馬上改變或一定採取行動。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是實際種植，也不必有操控或惡意；一次正面談話也能啟發想法。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述某次接觸如何引發日後的興趣或計劃。

listening.en: A visit to the repair café planted a seed in my mind, and months later I started learning to fix things.
listening.zh: 一次到維修咖啡室的參觀，在我心中種下了想法；幾個月後，我開始學習修理物品。
listening.promptZh: 參觀與後來學習有甚麼關係？

options.en: The visit introduced an idea that developed later.
options.zh: 參觀引發了一個後來才發展的想法。

options.en: The speaker immediately became an expert repairer.
options.zh: 說話者立即成為維修專家。

options.en: The visit confirmed a long-standing plan rather than introducing an idea.
options.zh: 參觀只是確認早已有的計劃，並非帶來新想法。

options.en: The speaker forgot the visit and saw no link to learning repairs.
options.zh: 說話者忘了參觀，也不認為它與學習維修有關。

listening.explanationZh: months later 顯示這是想法的開端，後來才付諸學習。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：你怎麼開始考慮開設社區書角？
reply.promptEn: How did you start thinking about a community book corner?

options.en: A neighbour's story gave me the initial idea.
options.zh: 鄰居的故事給了我最初的想法。

options.en: Seeing an unused shelf made me think about sharing books.
options.zh: 看見閒置書架，令我想到分享書本。

options.en: A conversation planted a seed in my mind, and I kept thinking about it.
options.zh: 一次談話在我心中種下想法，之後我一直想着它。

options.en: The idea began with a small discussion at our meeting.
options.zh: 這個想法源於會議上一段簡短討論。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都能交代想法的開始；金句加入種子的比喻。

scene.promptZh: 小學生聽過天文學家的分享，當時只覺得有趣；多年後選修天文學，想起那次分享。哪句最合適？

options.en: The talk planted a seed in her mind.
options.zh: 那次分享在她心中種下了想法。

options.en: The talk forced an immediate final career decision.
options.zh: 那次分享迫使她立即作出最終職業決定。

options.en: The talk completed a course of training she had already begun.
options.zh: 那次分享完成了她早已開始的培訓課程。

scene.explanationZh: 最初的啟發在多年後發展，符合種子慢慢成長的比喻。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個說法最不符合 plant a seed in their mind？

options.en: An idea may begin before it turns into action.
options.zh: 想法可以先出現，之後才變成行動。

options.en: The expression guarantees an immediate decision.
options.zh: 這個表達保證對方立即作決定。

options.en: An encouraging conversation can introduce a possibility.
options.zh: 鼓勵性的談話可以帶出一種可能性。

contrast.explanationZh: 種子比喻只說明開始與發展的可能，不保證即時決定。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我提議辦讀書會，但她沒有立刻答應，是不是完全沒用？」哪句最合適？

options.en: You may have planted a seed in her mind. Give her time to think.
options.zh: 你可能已在她心中種下想法。給她一點時間思考吧。

options.en: If she did not agree immediately, she cannot consider it later.
options.zh: 如果她沒有立即答應，以後就不可能考慮。

options.en: Planting a seed guarantees she will organise the group tomorrow.
options.zh: 種下想法就保證她明天會籌辦小組。

dialogue.explanationZh: may 保留可能性，鼓勵耐心，不替對方保證結果。

speaking.en: That conversation planted a seed in my mind about studying abroad.
speaking.zh: 那次談話在我心中種下了到外地升學的想法。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明一次談話如何引發想法。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友介紹屋頂種植，你當時沒有行動，幾星期後卻開始研究在家種植，並想付諸實行。用一至兩句英文交代最初的啟發與後來的行動。
writing.selfCheckZh: 連結最初的想法與較後的發展；不要把植入想法誤當保證立即行動。

examples.en: Her story planted a seed in my mind. A few weeks later, I began researching vegetables I could grow at home.
examples.zh: 她的故事在我心中種下了想法。幾星期後，我開始研究可以在家種甚麼蔬菜。

examples.en: The chat about rooftop gardens planted a seed in my mind, and I eventually tried growing herbs on the balcony.
examples.zh: 那次關於屋頂花園的聊天，在我心中種下想法；後來我終於嘗試在露台種香草。

takeaways.en: A simple question can plant a seed in your mind.
takeaways.zh: 一個簡單問題也能在你心中種下想法。

takeaways.en: The exhibition planted a seed in my mind about studying design.
takeaways.zh: 展覽在我心中種下了修讀設計的想法。

titleEn: at the forefront of their minds

brief.meaningEn: Among the most important things someone is actively thinking about.
brief.meaningZh: 是某人當下最重視、最常想到的事情之一。
brief.grammar: at/in the forefront of + possessive adjective + mind/minds; use mind for one person and normally minds for several people.
brief.register: Neutral to formal. The taught wording is the more established alternative to the source’s at the front of their mind.
brief.boundaryZh: 表示受到重視或正在思考，不代表唯一的想法，也不是物件實際位於腦部前面。
brief.misconceptionZh: 事情可以很重要而非令人焦慮；不必把這個表達一律翻成擔心。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明某個考慮因素如何持續受到重視。

listening.en: With the school trip approaching, the pupils’ safety was at the forefront of our minds.
listening.zh: 學校旅行將近，學生安全是我們最重視的事情之一。
listening.promptZh: 說話者籌備旅行時最重視甚麼？

options.en: Safety was a minor detail to be considered only after the trip.
options.zh: 安全是次要細節，只需旅行後才考慮。

options.en: Keeping pupils safe while planning the trip.
options.zh: 籌備旅行時確保學生安全。

options.en: The teachers had stopped considering every other part of the trip.
options.zh: 老師已停止考慮旅行的所有其他事項。

options.en: Forgetting that the trip was approaching.
options.zh: 忘記旅行快要來臨。

listening.explanationZh: 安全在籌備時受到高度重視；不是學生站在最前，也不表示沒有其他考慮。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：你們設計新圖書館時，最重視甚麼？
reply.promptEn: What matters most while you design the new library?

options.en: We want everyone to be able to use the space easily.
options.zh: 我們希望每個人都能方便使用這個空間。

options.en: Accessibility is at the forefront of our minds.
options.zh: 無障礙使用是我們最重視的事情之一。

options.en: We are paying close attention to different visitors' needs.
options.zh: 我們正仔細考慮不同訪客的需要。

options.en: Making the building welcoming is a major priority.
options.zh: 讓大樓親切易用是我們的重要優先事項。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都合理回答設計重點；金句表明一個持續受到重視的考慮因素。

scene.promptZh: 社區中心每次安排活動都先檢查輪椅通道，並聽取行動不便訪客的意見。哪句最準確？

options.en: Access is at the forefront of their minds.
options.zh: 無障礙使用是他們最重視的事情之一。

options.en: Access never enters their thinking.
options.zh: 他們從不考慮無障礙使用。

options.en: Access matters only when someone makes a complaint.
options.zh: 只有當有人投訴，無障礙使用才重要。

scene.explanationZh: 重複檢查與徵詢意見，顯示這個因素在計劃中受到高度重視。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不符合 at the forefront of their minds？

options.en: A team checks safety at every planning meeting.
options.zh: 團隊每次籌備會議都檢查安全。

options.en: A family regularly considers cost before making plans.
options.zh: 家庭制定計劃前經常考慮費用。

options.en: Organisers repeatedly forget a need and never discuss it.
options.zh: 主辦者反覆忘記某項需要，從未討論它。

contrast.explanationZh: 經常忘記、從不討論，與持續重視相反。

dialogue.promptZh: 同事說：「我們一直重視成本，難道代表只考慮錢？」哪句最準確？

options.en: Cost can be at the forefront of our minds without being our only concern.
options.zh: 成本可以是我們最重視的因素之一，但不是唯一考慮。

options.en: Anything at the forefront excludes every other concern.
options.zh: 只要某件事最受重視，就會排除所有其他考慮。

options.en: If cost is a priority, we cannot reconsider our plans.
options.zh: 如果成本是優先考慮，我們就不能重新考慮計劃。

dialogue.explanationZh: 重要程度高，不等於唯一因素；這是思考與重視的比喻。

speaking.en: Fairness is at the forefront of my mind when I divide the work.
speaking.zh: 分配工作時，公平是我最重視的事情之一。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明分工時最重視的因素。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你的小組準備戶外義賣，天氣很熱，大家每次討論都先考慮義工是否有水和遮蔭。用一至兩句英文說明你們的重點與安排。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出持續受到重視的因素，再用實際安排支持；不要聲稱這是唯一可考慮的事情。

examples.en: The volunteers' comfort is at the forefront of our minds. We will provide water and a shaded rest area.
examples.zh: 義工是否舒適是我們最重視的事情之一。我們會提供飲用水和有遮蔭的休息區。

examples.en: With the hot weather approaching, safety is at the forefront of our minds, so we are planning regular breaks.
examples.zh: 炎熱天氣將至，安全是我們最重視的事情之一，所以我們正在安排定時休息。

takeaways.en: Safety should be at the forefront of our minds when we plan the event.
takeaways.zh: 籌備活動時，安全應是我們最重視的事情之一。

takeaways.en: The needs of new visitors are at the forefront of their minds.
takeaways.zh: 新訪客的需要是他們最重視的事情之一。

brief.meaningEn: Begin to seem or be experienced in a particular way.
brief.meaningZh: 開始令人覺得如何，或開始產生某種感受。
brief.grammar: it starts to feel + adjective/like + noun; tense and subject can change. Feel can express perception rather than touch.
brief.register: Common natural sentence pattern, not an idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: 感覺的改變不等於客觀事實已改變；feels safe 不保證真的安全。
brief.misconceptionZh: feel 不只指用手觸摸；也不要把 starts to feel 誤解成已經一直如此。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述熟悉感或其他感受逐漸出現。

sources.sentence: When people see the same brand again and again, whether on social media, in videos, or on billboards, it starts to feel familiar and trustworthy.

listening.en: After a few friendly conversations, the new office started to feel less intimidating.
listening.zh: 幾次友善交談後，新辦公室開始讓人覺得沒那麼令人畏懼。
listening.promptZh: 說話者描述了甚麼變化？

options.en: The office had become objectively safe in every possible way.
options.zh: 辦公室已經在每個可能方面都客觀地安全。

options.en: The office had always felt exactly the same.
options.zh: 辦公室給人的感覺一直完全相同。

options.en: Friendly contact began to make the place seem less frightening.
options.zh: 友善接觸開始令這個地方感覺沒那麼可怕。

options.en: The office felt welcoming before any of the friendly conversations took place.
options.zh: 友善交談發生前，辦公室已經令人覺得親切。

listening.explanationZh: started 標示感覺開始改變；沒有說建築物改變或證明完全無風險。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：為甚麼你每天來這裏後，沒那麼緊張了？
reply.promptEn: Why are you less nervous after coming here every day?

options.en: I know a few people here now.
options.zh: 我現在認識這裏幾個人了。

options.en: The routine is becoming familiar.
options.zh: 這個日常安排正變得熟悉。

options.en: I have learned where things are and who to ask.
options.zh: 我已知道東西在哪裏，也知道可以問誰。

options.en: It starts to feel more welcoming when I see familiar faces.
options.zh: 看見熟悉面孔時，這裏開始讓人覺得更親切。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都能解釋緊張減少；金句描述地方帶來的感覺開始改變。

scene.promptZh: 剛搬家時你覺得房間很陌生，放好書本和照片後，開始有家的感覺。哪句最合適？

options.en: It started to feel like home after I unpacked.
options.zh: 我整理行李後，這裏開始有家的感覺。

options.en: It felt exactly the same before and after everything changed.
options.zh: 一切改變前後，它的感覺完全一樣。

options.en: I had finished every change to the room and would never alter it again.
options.zh: 我已完成房間的所有改動，永遠不會再改。

scene.explanationZh: 句子描述感受開始轉變，而不是法律擁有權。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句最清楚區分感覺與事實？

options.en: If it starts to feel trustworthy, it must be trustworthy.
options.zh: 只要它開始讓人覺得可靠，就一定可靠。

options.en: It starts to feel familiar, but I still need to check the facts.
options.zh: 它開始讓人覺得熟悉，但我仍要查證事實。

options.en: It must have been familiar from the beginning if it feels familiar now.
options.zh: 既然現在感覺熟悉，它一定從一開始就很熟悉。

contrast.explanationZh: 熟悉感與可靠程度不同；這個句式只交代感受，不自動證明事實。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「這個網站我看過很多次，現在覺得可信，可以不用查資料吧？」哪句最合宜？

options.en: It starts to feel familiar with repetition, but familiarity is not proof.
options.zh: 反覆接觸會開始令它感覺熟悉，但熟悉感不是證據。

options.en: If it feels familiar, every claim on it must be true.
options.zh: 只要感覺熟悉，網站上每個說法就一定是真的。

options.en: Seeing it often means I have already checked all its claims.
options.zh: 經常看見它，就表示我已查證它的所有說法。

dialogue.explanationZh: 承認重複接觸會改變感受，同時提醒仍要查證。

speaking.en: After a few visits, it starts to feel like a place where I belong.
speaking.zh: 去過幾次後，這裏開始讓我覺得有歸屬感。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述到訪幾次後逐漸出現的感覺。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你初次參加社區合唱團時很緊張，但幾次排練後，大家記得你的名字，也會跟你聊天。用一至兩句英文描述感覺的改變。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用具體互動支持感受改變；句式後接形容詞或 like 加名詞，不要誤寫成客觀保證。

examples.en: It started to feel more welcoming after a few rehearsals. People remembered my name and chatted with me.
examples.zh: 幾次排練後，這裏開始讓人覺得更親切。大家記得我的名字，也會跟我聊天。

examples.en: Now that I know the other singers, it starts to feel like a friendly community.
examples.zh: 現在我認識了其他歌手，這裏開始讓人覺得像個友善的社群。

takeaways.en: With practice, it starts to feel less unfamiliar.
takeaways.zh: 隨着練習，它開始讓人覺得沒那麼陌生。

takeaways.en: After several rehearsals, it starts to feel more natural.
takeaways.zh: 經過幾次排練後，它開始讓人覺得更自然。

titleEn: nudge people in a certain direction

target.pattern: \bnudg(?:e|es|ed|ing) (?:people|me|you|him|her|us|them|students|customers) in (?:a certain|that|this|a particular) direction\b|\bnudged in (?:a certain|that|this|a particular) direction\b

brief.meaningEn: Gently or subtly influence someone towards a choice or course of action.
brief.meaningZh: 以輕微或不明顯的方式，影響某人的選擇方向。
brief.grammar: nudge + object + in a certain/particular direction; be nudged in a certain direction is the passive form, with the influenced person as subject. The image is based on a gentle physical push.
brief.register: Neutral discussion of choices, design and persuasion.
brief.boundaryZh: 表示影響而非強迫；受影響的人仍可能作不同選擇，也不一定完全沒察覺。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不等於把人實際推向某處，也不保證影響一定成功。
brief.outcomeZh: 能辨認輕微提示或安排如何影響決定。

listening.en: Putting the healthier meals first can nudge customers in a certain direction without removing the other choices.
listening.zh: 先展示較健康的餐點，可以輕微引導顧客的選擇，而不用取消其他選項。
listening.promptZh: 這種安排的作用是甚麼？

options.en: It gently encourages one choice while keeping alternatives.
options.zh: 它輕微鼓勵某種選擇，同時保留其他選項。

options.en: It forces every customer to order the same meal.
options.zh: 它迫使每位顧客點同一餐。

options.en: It guarantees that healthier meals will become a favourite for everyone.
options.zh: 它保證較健康餐點會成為每個人的最愛。

options.en: It hides the healthier meals so customers consider them last.
options.zh: 它把較健康餐點藏起來，讓顧客最後才考慮。

listening.explanationZh: 沒有取消選擇，只用展示次序影響選擇傾向，符合輕微引導。

reply.promptZh: 朋友問：為甚麼網站把節能選項放在最上面？
reply.promptEn: Why does the website put the energy-saving option at the top?

options.en: It makes that option easier to notice.
options.zh: 這令那個選項較容易被留意。

options.en: It may encourage visitors to consider it first.
options.zh: 這可能鼓勵訪客先考慮它。

options.en: The layout can nudge people in a certain direction while leaving the choice open.
options.zh: 版面可以輕微引導人們的選擇方向，同時保留選擇自由。

options.en: The designers want to make the lower-energy choice more visible.
options.zh: 設計者想讓較節能的選項更顯眼。

reply.explanationZh: 四個回應都解釋版面影響；金句清楚區分引導與強制。

scene.promptZh: 圖書館把推薦書放在入口，仍讓讀者自由選其他書。哪句最準確？

options.en: The display may nudge people in a certain direction.
options.zh: 陳列方式可能會輕微引導人們的選擇方向。

options.en: The display removes every reader's choice.
options.zh: 陳列方式令每位讀者都失去選擇。

options.en: The display guarantees that everyone will borrow the same book.
options.zh: 陳列方式保證每個人都借同一本書。

scene.explanationZh: 增加顯眼程度是輕微影響，不等於限制選擇或保證結果。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不像 nudge people in a certain direction？

options.en: A gentle reminder encourages students to bring reusable bottles.
options.zh: 溫和提醒鼓勵學生帶可重用水瓶。

options.en: An organiser removes every alternative and requires everyone to make the same choice.
options.zh: 主辦者取消所有其他選項，要求每人作同一選擇。

options.en: A clear label makes a lower-cost option more noticeable.
options.zh: 清晰標籤令較便宜的選項更顯眼。

contrast.explanationZh: 取消選項並強制同一選擇，超出了輕微引導的意思。

dialogue.promptZh: 同事說：「只要把這個選項放前面，人人都會選它。」哪句回應最準確？

options.en: It may nudge people in that direction, but it will not decide for everyone.
options.zh: 這可能輕微引導人們朝那個方向選擇，但不會替每個人作決定。

options.en: A nudge guarantees the same decision from every person.
options.zh: 輕微引導保證每個人作相同決定。

options.en: The order of options can never influence anyone.
options.zh: 選項次序絕不可能影響任何人。

dialogue.explanationZh: may 和不保證人人相同，準確表達影響程度。

speaking.en: A friendly reminder can nudge us in a certain direction without forcing a decision.
speaking.zh: 友善提醒可以輕微引導我們的選擇方向，而不強迫作決定。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明提醒與強迫的分別。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：學校想鼓勵學生多用樓梯，在樓梯旁放上友善提示，但仍開放升降機。用一至兩句英文描述提示的作用，並保留學生的選擇。
writing.selfCheckZh: 說明輕微引導及具體方法，並保留其他選擇；不用保證所有人都照做。

examples.en: The signs may nudge students in a certain direction by making the stairs more noticeable. The lift remains available.
examples.zh: 提示牌把樓梯變得更顯眼，可能會輕微引導學生的選擇。升降機仍然開放。

examples.en: A friendly message can nudge people in a certain direction, but students should still be free to choose the lift.
examples.zh: 友善訊息可以輕微引導人們的選擇方向，但學生仍應可自由選擇乘升降機。

takeaways.en: A small change can nudge people in a certain direction.
takeaways.zh: 一個小改變可以輕微引導人們的選擇方向。

takeaways.en: A clear label can nudge people in a certain direction without removing alternatives.
takeaways.zh: 清晰的標籤可以輕微引導人們的選擇方向，而不用取消其他選項。
